newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo Trust disposed of 460 bln yen problem loans.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo Trust disposed of 460 bln yen problem loans.

text.p: Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd said on Monday that it disposed of an estimated 460 billion yen in problem loans in the business year that ended on March 31.
The bank said the amount included provisions worth 60 billion yen set aside to cover expected losses on loans it provided to three failed financial firms affiliated with Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
Sumitomo Trust said in a statement that its loans outstanding to the three NCB affiliates totalled about 101 billion yen.

Earlier on Monday, the Tokyo District Court said that a bankruptcy filing by the three affiliates had been accepted. NCB, a troubled long-term credit bank, said on April 1 that the affiliates had filed for bankruptcy as part of a restructuring.

Sumitomo Trust said that because of the bankruptcy filing it decided to set aside loan loss provisions related to the three affiliates, resulting in a downward revision of its parent current profit forecast for 1996/97 to 12 billion yen from the previous forecast of 100 billion yen.
The bank also said that it posted a 51.0 billion yen appraisal loss on securities holdings.

The estimated disposal of problem loans in 1996/97 included additional loan loss provisions for problem loans extended to Japan's Cooperative Credit Purchasing Co Ltd (CCPC), Sumitomo Trust said. The CCPC was set up by financial institutions four years ago to buy problem loans and recover them, in order to speed up their disposal.
Sumitomo Trust is scheduled to announce its 1996/97 business results in late May.
